name: Canon EOS R5
note: Canon's high-resolution full-frame RF flagship line. Two generations in this dataset: EOS R5 (marketed July 2020) and EOS R5 Mark II (marketed August 2024). Canon's own model naming states the generation.

name: Canon EOS R6
note: Canon's full-frame RF enthusiast line. EOS R6 (marketed August 2020) and EOS R6 Mark II (marketed December 2022).

name: Canon EOS R1 / R3
note: Canon's integrated-grip professional RF bodies: EOS R3 (marketed November 2021) and EOS R1 (marketed November 2024). Grouped by shared body form and stacked-sensor description; Canon's naming does not make R1 a numbered successor to R3, so no successor_of edge is asserted between them.

name: Canon EOS R APS-C (R7 / R10 / R50 / R100)
note: RF-mount APS-C bodies. Canon's specification tables give the sensor as approx. 22.3 x 14.8 mm (R7) or 22.3 x 14.9 mm (R10, R50, R100) and list RF-S lenses as compatible.

name: Canon EOS R / RP / R8
note: Canon's smaller full-frame RF bodies without in-body stabilisation: EOS R (October 2018), EOS RP (March 2019), EOS R8 (April 2023). Grouped by segment, not by a Canon-stated succession.

name: Canon EOS EF-mount DSLRs
note: EF and EF-S mount digital SLRs still widely used: EOS 6D Mark II, EOS 90D, EOS 250D, EOS 2000D. All state an optical viewfinder and a dedicated phase-detection AF sensor with a published point count.

name: Nikon Z9 / Z8
note: Nikon's 45.7 MP FX bodies with identical sensor description (35.9 x 23.9 mm CMOS), 493 focus points and 8K UHD 30p video. The Z9 has an integrated grip and EN-EL18d battery; the Z8 is the smaller EN-EL15c body.

name: Nikon Z6
note: Nikon's 24.5 MP FX line. Only the Z6III is in this dataset with specifications; Nikon's lineup index also lists Z6 and Z6II, whose specification pages were not reachable in this pass.

name: Nikon Z5
note: Nikon's entry full-frame FX line. Z5II captured here; Nikon's lineup index also lists the Z5.

name: Nikon Z50
note: Nikon's DX-format enthusiast line. Z50II captured here; Nikon's lineup index also lists the Z50.

name: Nikon Zf / Zfc
note: Nikon's heritage-styled Z bodies: Zf (FX, 24.5 MP, with a Vibration reduction section in its specification) and Zfc (DX, 20.9 MP, without one). Same design language, different formats — no succession is asserted between them.

name: Nikon Z30
note: DX-format Z body whose specification table lists no viewfinder at all.

name: Nikon F-mount DSLRs
note: Only the D780 has a reachable manufacturer specification page in this pass. Nikon's DSLR lineup index also lists D6, D850, D500 and D3500.

name: Sony Alpha 1
note: Sony's 50.1 MP full-frame Exmor RS flagship line: Alpha 1 (ILCE-1) and Alpha 1 II (ILCE-1M2). Sony's own model codes state the generation.

name: Sony Alpha 9
note: Sony's speed-oriented full-frame line. Only the Alpha 9 III (ILCE-9M3) is in this dataset — notable for a base ISO of 250 rather than 100.

name: Sony Alpha 7
note: Sony's full-frame all-rounder line: Alpha 7 IV (ILCE-7M4) and Alpha 7 V (ILCE-7M5), both 33 MP, the 7 V on an Exmor RS sensor where the 7 IV uses Exmor R.

name: Sony Alpha 7R
note: Sony's high-resolution full-frame line. Alpha 7R V (ILCE-7RM5), 61 MP Exmor R.

name: Sony Alpha 7S
note: Sony's low-light/video full-frame line. Alpha 7S III (ILCE-7SM3), 12.1 MP, with the widest ISO range in this dataset (80-102400, expanded 40-409600).

name: Sony Alpha 7C
note: Sony's compact full-frame line. Alpha 7C II (ILCE-7CM2), 33 MP, sharing the 7 IV's sensor description in a 514 g body.

name: Sony Alpha APS-C (a6000 series)
note: E-mount APS-C bodies: Alpha 6400 (ILCE-6400, 24.2 MP Exmor, no stabilisation figure) and Alpha 6700 (ILCE-6700, 26 MP Exmor R with a 5.0-stop stabilisation claim).

name: Sony ZV
note: Sony's video-first E-mount bodies. ZV-E10 II (ZV-E10M2) shares the Alpha 6700's sensor description and has no viewfinder — Sony's table lists the viewfinder as "-".

name: Fujifilm X-T
note: Fujifilm's dial-led APS-C line. X-T5, 40.2 MP X-Trans CMOS 5 HR with X-Processor 5.

name: Fujifilm X-H
note: Fujifilm's flagship APS-C line, split by sensor: X-H2 (40.2 MP X-Trans CMOS 5 HR, 8K video) and X-H2S (26.16 MP X-Trans CMOS 5 HS, 6.2K). Identical body dimensions and weight; both pair CFexpress Type B with SD UHS-II.

name: Fujifilm X-S
note: Fujifilm's compact mode-dial APS-C line. X-S20, 26.1 MP X-Trans CMOS 4 with X-Processor 5.

name: Fujifilm X100
note: Fixed-lens APS-C compact with a hybrid optical/electronic viewfinder. X100VI: 40.2 MP X-Trans CMOS 5 HR behind a fixed 23mm F2.0 lens — no interchangeable mount, so its mount field is null.
